<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via buildReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SharingService))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`  _(via buildReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SharingService))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`  _(via buildReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SharingService), buildWriteFilter (symbol, a method of class SharingService))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 273137d227f79ac91b783bc3d25f09e51e7bad4e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9806e8adbd649d646109e8eeff75ac9013e0d1ee` — the merge of head `9cc5f83a65a200f4be69921b3e0a50c69db3cf28` into base `273137d227f79ac91b783bc3d25f09e51e7bad4e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9806e8adbd649d646109e8eeff75ac9013e0d1ee && git checkout 9806e8adbd649d646109e8eeff75ac9013e0d1ee
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 273137d227f79ac91b783bc3d25f09e51e7bad4e 9cc5f83a65a200f4be69921b3e0a50c69db3cf28 && git checkout -B drift-repro 273137d227f79ac91b783bc3d25f09e51e7bad4e && git merge --no-ff 9cc5f83a65a200f4be69921b3e0a50c69db3cf28

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 273137d227f79ac91b783bc3d25f09e51e7bad4e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 273137d227f79ac91b783bc3d25f09e51e7bad4e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Not reviewed (prose faces, read only to judge the narrowing's wording): .changeset/27425-phantom-owner-anchor-fails-closed.md, content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx. PR not merged at review time (`merged: false`, head unchanged); the diff on the local ref `prr-27476` against `origin/main` is byte-identical to `net.diff` (11 files, +375/-57).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`SharingService.buildReadFilter`, unproven owner anchor, caller below `org` read depth, OWD `private` for the principal** — `null` (no scope) becomes `{ id: '__deny_all__' }`, or `{ id: { $in: approvalIds } }` when the approvals service vouches for pending-approver reads. **Right.** The check sits after the `org` early return and after the principal-less deny, so it cannot widen anything: the owner arm, the share-row arm (`sys_record_share`) and the queue arm (ADR-0142) are all dropped, the approval arm alone survives, and that arm is an id list the approvals service already fails closed on (no service, on-behalf-of, a throw ⇒ none). The spec's `sharingModel: 'private'` is "owner-only" (object.zod.ts:3237); this makes that refusal real where it was not.
2. **`buildWriteFilter`, same class, below `org` write depth** — `null` becomes `{ id: '__deny_all__' }`. **Right.** The by-id gates (`checkEdit` / `checkDelete` via `matchesOwnerScope`) already refuse every row of such an object (`owner == null`); the bulk filter was wider than the by-id gates on `main`, and the narrowing closes that asymmetry. The dev declared it as a deviation and the PM accepted it (card comment 6491005449).
3. **`hasPhantomOwnerAnchor` answers `false` when `external.columnMap` has `owner_id` as a value** (`mapsRemoteColumnOntoOwner`). This moves the mapped-but-undeclared class out of the phantom set, with three derived effects:
   - **Reads / bulk writes** on that class scope over `owner_id` (own + shares + queue), where `main` left reads unscoped. **Right.** The spec declares `columnMap` as "Remote column name → local field name" (object.zod.ts:1375), so a value of `owner_id` is declared metadata naming the remote owner column; this is still "proven from declared metadata", the triage bar. On a built-in SQL driver the map is applied on the WHERE (`remoteColumn`, sql-driver.ts:15286, used at 14204/14620/14875), ORDER BY and the read output (`formatOutput`, 17791), and the real-stack pin shows own-only. On a plugin driver, which does not apply the map, the datasource is floored (`needsExternalDriverFloor`: `schemaMode !== 'managed'` and a driver id no built-in resolves) and `applyDriverQueryInMemory` re-applies the `where` over the returned rows (`matchesDriverWhere`); a row with no `owner_id` key matches no owner predicate, so the scope stays closed. The fail direction is closed on both driver kinds.
   - **`grant()` on that class is no longer refused as inert** (`inertGrantReason` reads `hasPhantomOwnerAnchor`), and the external-recipient arm of a public model admits it too. **Right in direction** (the share row IS now consulted: the read filter ORs `{ id: { $in: grantedIds } }`, an id arm that holds on both driver kinds), but it is a change the changeset does not name — see ② and ④ should-fix 2.
   - **`notePhantomAnchorWriteDeny` (#8418) no longer logs** for a mapped object on a driver that ignores the map. Verdict-free by construction, so no gate moves; the lint warning still names the shape at authoring time. Carried by the seat on the epic (ACCEPT §5); see ④ should-fix 3.
4. **`org` read depth still returns `null`** before the phantom check, and View All / Modify All resolve to `org` (permission-evaluator.ts:311, 352). **Right, and not a bypass**: `org` depth reads an object without an owner predicate on every object, declared-owner federated ones included; the ADR-0057 depth semantics are unchanged. `unit` / `unit_and_below` / `own_and_reports` all reach the phantom check before `resolveOwnerScopeIds` and are pinned to deny-all; `owning_business_unit_id` is composed into no read or write predicate anywhere in plugin-sharing or plugin-security (card task 3 answered).
5. **Principal-less context on this class now reaches the existing deny-all; an external principal on a `public_read` phantom object is floored to owner-only and then deny-all; guest and delegated (on-behalf-of) paths compose by AND and stay deny-all.** **Right**, each pinned in `federated-phantom-owner-scoping.test.ts`.
6. **Lint `security-external-owner-unmapped` message**: the owner arm on effective `private` now reads "refused (404: the member's read scope admits no row)"; `public_read`, and the `created_by` arm (any `ownership` tier other than `user`), keep "(403)". **Right**: on `private` the scoped pre-image read finds no row ⇒ `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`; on `public_read` the read is open and the write gate refuses ⇒ 403; without `owner_id` sharing abstains and the floor refuses ⇒ 403. Advisory text, no accept-set change. The `os explain` entry's two amended sentences agree with the code.
7. **Runtime spike (e3)**: a member PATCH on the default-model external object now pins 404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, no `driver.update`, and the scoped pre-image read carries the deny sentinel in its `$and`. **Right** per the middleware composition on head.
8. **Managed (local) objects and declared-owner federated objects**: `hasPhantomOwnerAnchor` is `false` for both on every path (`isFederatedObject` short-circuit; `equalsShippedDef` identity against `OWNER_FIELD_DEF`), so their filters are byte-for-byte unchanged. The in-repo external objects `showcase_ext_customer` / `showcase_ext_order` are `public_read_write` and never reach the owner arm.

**Read doors checked for a bypass of the new check** (the security rule): `find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate` all enter the sharing middleware (sharing-plugin.ts:1351); REST list / by-id / related-list reads, `GET /data/:object/export` and `GET /search` read through the engine under the caller's resolved context; the analytics raw-SQL door takes `security.getReadFilter` → `resolveSharingReadFilter` → `buildReadFilter`; `packages/mcp` holds no direct driver read; share links are redeemed at their own door and never through this filter. No read door bypasses the narrowed filter. The `__deny_all__` sentinel is a plain id equality, so a SQL driver matches no row and a floored plugin driver's rows are re-filtered in memory.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/27425-phantom-owner-anchor-fails-closed.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-sharing: patch`, `@objectstack/lint: patch`; line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the changeset and the PR body; `BREAKING` banner; one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). AGENTS.md step 3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no authorable key, value or default changes; the remedy is an existing metadata choice). **Level matches the diff.** `Check Changeset` and the queue guard are green on the head.
- The `Clause-②` sentence says "Nothing is widened". The narrowing is faithfully described, but the diff also stops refusing `grant()` on a mapped-but-undeclared federated object (①.3), which is a published service method whose refusal set shrinks for one object class. Should-fix (wording): name it in the changeset, and let the seat decide whether the arm reads `yes (narrowing)` under record-recognisers' "a diff that widens and narrows owes the narrowing review" rule. Not a FAIL: the direction follows the contract's own criterion (a share row that can be consulted is not inert), the share arm is an id list that holds on both driver kinds, and no exposure results.
- The `(narrowing)` arm owes the PR body a third line, `Skills-docs: …` (pm-dispatch SKILL.md L313; review-checklist L18). The PR body carries none. `skills/**` teaches nothing about external-object sharing (searched on `main`), and the docs are updated in this diff, so the honest value is `updated here` or `none — REASON`. Escalated to the seat as should-fix 4; a PR-body line, no code change.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report (card comment 6492305231): `open_questions: []`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. Nothing to answer.
- Five declared deviations, each checked against the diff and each covered by a PM claim amendment on the card: (1) bulk write filter narrowed — in the diff, accepted 07:45Z; (2) `columnMap` onto `owner_id` counts as declared — in the diff, accepted 07:56Z; (3) files outside plugin-sharing — exactly the lint rule + message + test, the `os explain` entry, the two guide passages and spike (e3), as amendments 1 and 2 name; (4) `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with BREAKING banner where the dispatch said `Clause-②: no` — the arm the banner requires; (5) census — `showcase_ext_customer` and `showcase_ext_order` are `public_read_write` (verified on `main`), no example file changed.
- Seat ACCEPT (PR comment 09:41Z) carries two out-of-scope findings to the epic: the lost write-deny diagnostic on a mapped object over a map-ignoring driver, and the duplicated `columnMap` reader (lint `columnMapTargets` and plugin-sharing `mapsRemoteColumnOntoOwner`). Both are real and both are should-fix grade; see ④.
- Docs-drift bot flagged `content/docs/kernel/index.mdx`, `kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`, `permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx`. Read on `main`: the one sentence about federated objects (sharing-service.mdx L63, the `SHARING_NOT_ENABLED` arm: "the platform's injected anchor rather than a real remote column") stays true under the `columnMap` arm, since a mapped column is a real remote column. No sentence made false.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); no out-of-relay author to name.
- Check-runs on `9cc5f83a65a200f4be69921b3e0a50c69db3cf28`: 51 runs, 42 `success`, 9 `skipped` (matrix placeholders and opt-in harnesses), 0 failed, 0 pending. These are the gate verdicts; nothing was run locally.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** `sharingModel: 'private'` is declared as owner-only (object.zod.ts:3237), and a federated object omitting it resolves to `private` (ADR-0090 D1, `effectiveSharingModel`). On `main` the #7858 branch read an unproven owner anchor as "ownership contributes nothing" and returned `null`, so on this class the declared refusal was not real. The head makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away at the consumer: no author was ever promised that `private` reads every row, and the two remedies the guide now names (`public_read`, or declare / map the owner column) are both inside the published spec. The mechanism: provenance decided from declared metadata (`fields.owner_id` or a `columnMap` value `owner_id`), and on every path where it cannot be proven the scope narrows below `org` and never widens; the pins are the two phantom-scoping suites (filter shape at every depth; rows-level over the sharing double for a plugin driver serving an undeclared owner, a map-applying driver, a map-ignoring driver and a declared control), the real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` suite (served-undeclared, mapped, declared, with a premise case), the spike (e3) and the lint wording case.

**Attempts to break it, each closed in the live tree:** a read door around the middleware (none: ①'s door list); a plugin driver that ignores `where` (the #27277 floor re-applies it in memory, including the sentinel equality and the owner predicate); the mapped arm on a map-ignoring driver (no `owner_id` key on the row ⇒ the owner predicate admits nothing); delegated reads (AND-composed, delegator leg has no approval grants); the queue arm (dropped on this class; the `queue` column is as unprovisioned as `owner_id`); `unit` depths (phantom check precedes the hierarchy resolver); principal-less and guest (deny-all first); `org` depth (unchanged and the same on declared-owner objects — View All semantics, not a bypass); a `columnMap` naming a remote column that does not exist (a SQL error or zero rows, never exposure).

**Findings** — none is must-fix:

1. **Should-fix — the spec's provenance convergence row now diverges.** `injected-system-column-provenance.ts` names #7858 as "the `owner_id` twin of #7859", i.e. plugin-sharing converging on `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance(schema, 'owner_id') === 'injected-unprovisioned'`. For a mapped-but-undeclared object the spec helper answers `injected-unprovisioned` (lint therefore still warns, correctly) while plugin-sharing now scopes over the mapped column. Both are fail-closed, so nothing opens; but the convergence map should record the `columnMap` exception (or the helper should learn the arm) so the next consumer that converges does not silently re-widen or re-narrow this class. Done-when: the spec module's convergence map names the `columnMap` arm, or `resolveInjectedColumnProvenance` takes it and plugin-sharing reads the helper.
2. **Should-fix — the changeset's "Nothing is widened" and the `grant()` accept set** (②). Done-when: the changeset names that a grant on a federated object whose `columnMap` maps a remote column onto `owner_id` is now accepted, and the seat rules on the `Clause-②` arm.
3. **Should-fix — the #8418 write-deny diagnostic goes silent on a mapped object over a map-ignoring plugin driver** (`notePhantomAnchorWriteDeny` keys on `hasPhantomOwnerAnchor`). The refusal stands (owner read is `null`), only the operator's one-line diagnosis is lost; the lint warning still names the shape at authoring time. Already carried by the seat on the epic.
